4 · Sky's notes, and where each is answered

Sky saidAnswered by
"nothing showing me what the cell player is doing when they're busy"An activity strip per agent (icon, plain label, progress bar, time left, queued next act, READY / BUSY / HURT / DOWN) and the same in the street: an icon with a progress ring and a dotted line to the destination with a time flag. Frames 3, 7, 9.
"nor is there a way to cancel their action"An x on the strip and on the in-world ring (selected agent), with a hover card saying what it costs to stop, and Backspace. Frame 3.
"nothing telling me about the mission"The briefing card at the start (objective, target, win, lose, close 8:30, purse, the two approaches) and an objective line under the pill for the whole run. Frames 1 to 10.
"very unclear on what to do"A dismissible next-step hint that names the agent, the key and the target and ringed target in the street (frames 2, 4, 7), and Intel: who is known, what is known, the one next action that would learn more (frame 4).
"action panel too condensed, not enough dialogue"Action panel v2: one card per verb with a plain line about what it does and its trade-off, price, walk and outcome; locked cards say why and how to unlock (frame 5).
"dialogue shown, bottom left, that can collapse"The dialogue log, docked bottom-left: speaker chips, agent acknowledgements, replies, results and barks; collapsed it is one line (frame 6; one line in all others).

5 · What will matter most for clarity, and what to watch

  1. The activity strip is the answer to "what is my agent doing". Verb, bar, time left, and a cancel in one place per agent. If only one thing ships, ship this.
  2. Cancel needs honesty. The hover card must state what is lost (listening so far) and what is not spent. Cancelling a Fixer action after the money is paid has a different answer, which the engine must supply as text; this is a rules question for Motive and Keel, not art.
  3. Cost of clarity: screen. The docked HUD (column, strips, verb plate, pill, objective, log line) draws about 11 to 13% of the frame when something is open, 8% of it in the left dock. Round 5b's bare roster was 2.7%. Frame 12 (strips only for busy agents) brings the left dock to 4.8%. My recommendation: ship 12 as the default and let a key (Tab) show every strip.
  4. Text length. Card lines run 100 to 130 characters. They read at 13.5 px on a 1080p screen but they are the first thing to cut or localise; Fable's text file should set the limit (about 110).
  5. The hint reads from state. It needs a trigger table (what the player has done, what is learned) from Motive or Waymark; the mock-up shows four. It must vanish the moment the player acts, never nag, and H hides it for good.
  6. Keys. The cancel key is shown as Backspace; verbs 1 to 4, agents F1 to F4, H hides the hint, C carries. All provisional until Sky plays.
  7. Dialogue. Ten lines fit expanded; the log keeps more on scroll. Barks (a guard's line, a rival's shout) are grey and short so results (seafoam bar) stand out. Speaker chips are the agent's own portrait, so the log doubles as a second roster glance.
  8. Fight state shows what GDD v0.22.0 asks: the crosshair, "hits 3 in 4 · down in 5.5 s", the 0.5 s hold ring on the going-loud card, health pips on the portraits and over every combatant, a downed agent with a carry prompt, and the stance icon on each strip. Final-fight shots read "untraced" on the chip.
  9. Not shown: the investigator question mark and its dotted lead line (no investigator in these beats), the pause and speed readout, the hover dossier card, the debrief detail.
